slot.brief: Alpha-numeric series combining letters with positional values and numbers following two interleaved rules; one term breaks the pattern — ask which term is wrong.

stem: One term in the following $\alpha-numeric$ series is wrong. Identify it: D-3, I-4, H-8, M-10, L-15, Q-18, P-24, U-27.

verdicts.working: Letters follow +5, −1 alternately. Numbers follow +1, +4, +2, +5, +3, +6, +4, so the last number should be 28, not 27.

working:
Odd- and even-position letters each advance by 4: D-H-L-P and I-M-Q-U. Odd-position numbers rise by +5, +7, +9: 3, 8, 15, 24. Even-position numbers rise by +6, +8, +10: 4, 10, 18, 28. Thus the last term should be U-28, so U-27 is wrong.

Independent check: Letters follow +5, −1 alternately. Numbers follow +1, +4, +2, +5, +3, +6, +4, so the last number should be 28, not 27.
solution:
The odd-position numbers increase by $+5,+7,+9$: $3,8,15,24$. The even-position numbers increase by $+6,+8,+10$: $4,10,18,28$.
Thus the last term should be $U$-$28$, so $U$-$27$ is incorrect.
